message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant genetic traits is the presence of a mane in adult males. The allele that codes for mane development is dominant over the allele that results in a maneless phenotype. Thus, if a male lion inherits at least one copy of the mane allele from either parent, it will develop a full mane.
